messages.content: What is the largest planet in the universe?

function.name: space_star_info
function.description: Retrieve information about a particular star in the universe. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

information.description: The type of information needed about the star.

message.content:
The largest planet that has been confirmed so far is **HD 100546 b**.  
It orbits the young star HD 100546 and has a radius roughly **2.5 × Jupiter’s radius** (about 18,000 km). Its mass is estimated at around **10–15 M_Jup**, making it one of the most massive “hot Jupiters” known.

Other very large exoplanets include:

| Exoplanet | Approximate radius | Approximate mass |
|-----------|--------------------|------------------|
| **HD 106906 b** | ~1.8 × Jupiter | ~11 M_Jup |
| **WASP‑17 b** | ~1.9 × Jupiter | ~0.5 M_Jup (but very low density) |

These objects are still within the planetary regime (below the deuterium‑burning limit of ~13 M_Jup). No confirmed planet larger than HD 100546 b has been found yet, though future surveys may discover even bigger worlds.
